top10.introHtml: Top 10 picks ranked as a cheap fun second car — condition and reliability over raw mileage. Verified clean title and no reported accidents on Cars.com listings. Oct 27, 2026 refresh.

picks.whyGood: Only 34k miles on a 2007 E90 3 Series convertible — that's exceptional low use. BMW's naturally-aspirated inline-six in the 328i is smooth, parts are everywhere, and the E93 hardtop is dead reliable when maintained. Sold by Scott Mazda, a franchise dealer, which adds some inspection confidence.
picks.whatToVerify: Operate the folding hardtop through a full open/close cycle — listen for motor strain or hesitation. Check headliner and rear-seat carpet for any water intrusion stains. Inspect rocker panels for rust blistering. Ask for service history: oil changes every 5k, any coolant or valve-cover gasket work. Confirm no CARFAX accidents beyond what's reported.
picks.bottomLine: Low-mile E93 at a franchise dealer — this is the standout find of the week.

picks.whyGood: The N54 twin-turbo straight-six in the 135i is one of BMW's great engines — 300 hp stock, tons of tuning headroom, and well-documented maintenance community. At 48k miles it's barely broken in for a German sports coupe. Price is fair for the spec.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) — ask if replaced or check for any fuel-cut symptoms. Check for wastegate rattle on cold start (common N54 quirk, usually benign). Fold top cycle check. Water pump and thermostat service history (common preventive items at 60k). Inspect for any boost-related leaks at intercooler pipes.
picks.bottomLine: Twin-turbo 135i at 48k miles for $12,590 is a serious performance deal — verify the fuel pump and enjoy.

picks.whyGood: F33 4 Series convertible with xDrive AWD and the N55 single-turbo six — this generation improved on the E93 in every measurable way. At $8,500 for a 435i it's priced purely on miles, but German six-cylinder convertibles regularly go 180k+ with proper maintenance. The folding hardtop is near-silent and rattle-free.
picks.whatToVerify: At 140k miles: check timing chain tensioner (known N55 item around this mileage), cooling system condition (water pump, expansion tank), and brake condition front and rear. Folding hardtop cycle — all latches secure, no wind noise. Check for oil leaks at valve cover and oil filter housing gasket.
picks.bottomLine: High miles but best-value modern BMW convertible in the batch — a solid bet if the maintenance records check out.

picks.whyGood: 51k-mile XK8 rated 'Great Deal' by Cars.com and just 28 miles away in Feasterville — very low mileage for a 2005 at this price point. The 4.2L naturally-aspirated V8 is silky, the interior is proper British luxury, and the X150 XK is a genuinely beautiful car. Verified clean title and no accidents.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for nikasil cylinder bore issues (less common on 2005+ but worth asking about), timing chain tensioner service, and coolant header tank condition. Inspect the convertible top hydraulic rams for leaks at the seals — slow top movement is a warning sign. Check for any electrical gremlins (window regulators, seat motor). Test all climate zones.
picks.bottomLine: Low-mile British V8 drop-top at a fair price nearby — one of the more characterful picks in this refresh.

picks.whyGood: E46 330Ci with only 64k miles — the M54 inline-six is one of BMW's best naturally-aspirated engines, smooth and long-lived. The E46 convertible's folding soft top is simpler and more reliable than the later E93/F33 folding hardtops. Verified clean title and no accidents.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for rear subframe cracking (common E46 issue — look at the subframe mounting points in the trunk). Inspect the soft top for rear window delamination and seam integrity. Oil and coolant system condition. Check for DISA valve failure symptoms (rough idle, hesitation). Confirm power top opens and latches fully.
picks.bottomLine: Classic E46 330 with low miles — fix the subframe if needed, and you have a great driver.

picks.whyGood: 2004 Ford Thunderbird revival with only 60k miles — these 11th-gen Birds use a smooth 3.9L V8 and are genuinely stylish. Low production numbers mean they hold value well as collectibles. Clean title + no accidents. Private seller pricing.
picks.whatToVerify: Check the removable hardtop storage bag condition and tonneau cover. Inspect for any coolant or oil seepage at the Jaguar-derived AJ-series V8. Verify the soft top seals (drivers report water intrusion at rear corners). Check for any rust at the rear quarter-panel seam — known weak point on these. AC operation.
picks.bottomLine: Retro collectible at a fair price — fun, comfortable, and genuinely distinctive.

picks.whyGood: 2016 A3 Cabriolet — the most modern, tech-equipped car in this refresh. Clean Audi interior, VW Group 2.0T which is plentiful for parts, and only 84k miles. The soft top on the 8V A3 Cabrio is well-regarded for sealing and durability.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for DSG transmission service history if equipped (7-speed DL501 service at 40k intervals). Inspect soft top seal at the windshield header. Verify MMI infotainment functions. Check for any carbon buildup symptoms on the direct-injection EA888 engine (common above 80k). Water drain channels below soft top rails should be clear.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern car here — clean, connected, and still under 90k miles.

picks.whyGood: Another very-low-mileage 135i — 48k miles, 22 miles away at Premier Auto Group. The N54 twin-turbo is the same engine as the rank-2 CarGurus listing; this one is at a dealer with slightly lower asking price.
picks.whatToVerify: Same N54 checklist as rank-2: HPFP history, wastegate rattle, boost pipe condition. Ask dealer for any service records. Check folding top operation. Inspect for prior body panel work (AutoTrader listing has no-accidents but dealer verification helps).
picks.bottomLine: Low-mile 135i close by — if rank-2 is already gone, this is the fallback.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest pick in the Top 10 at $7,094 — 99k miles on the simple, reliable 2.5L five-cylinder. The A5 Beetle Cabrio is a pleasant, easy-to-own convertible; parts are everywhere and mechanics know them well. Great entry point if you want a fun drop-top on a tight budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Inspect soft top for any tears or yellowing at the rear window. Check for any oil leaks from the 2.5L (generally robust but watch the valve cover gasket). Verify the convertible top motor operates at normal speed. Check for any rust at the A-pillar base seam. Coil pack condition (typical VW maintenance item).
picks.bottomLine: Best budget buy — low risk, parts are easy to find, and it's a fun daily at under $7,200.

picks.whyGood: 54k-mile 2002 Thunderbird at GT Motors, 25 miles away. Very low mileage for a 22-year-old collector car. These early revival Birds with under 60k miles are increasingly hard to find at this price.
picks.whatToVerify: Same checks as rank-6 Thunderbird: soft top rear corner sealing, V8 cooling system, hardtop storage. At 54k miles verify timing chain tensioner service hasn't been deferred. Check under-car for any rear quarter rust.
picks.bottomLine: A 54k-mile Thunderbird within 25 miles — solid collectable buy if the soft top seals check out.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles from 2000+ in budget. Ranked by trim and mileage — GT and V8 trims preferred over V6.

picks.whyGood: 2013 S197 V6 Mustang convertible with only 43k miles — the lowest-mileage Mustang convertible in this refresh. The 3.7L V6 makes 305 hp and is silky compared to the old V6. Verified clean title and no accidents via Cars.com. Sold by Highline Motor Cars.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 convertible top rear seal at the quarter window — common water entry point. Check rear seat carpet for moisture. Inspect for any rear axle clunk on takeoff (8.8 rear). Confirm top opens and latches at both front header clips. Ask about any service at common S197 mileage items: rear axle fluid, spark plugs.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest-mileage Mustang convertible of the week — best condition pick if you want a 'Stang.

picks.whyGood: 2014 last-year S197 V6 at $9,442 — budget-conscious pick 29 miles away. Good year for the S197 (refined over earlier model years). No accidents reported.
picks.whatToVerify: At 121k: check spark plugs, coil packs, and rear axle seal condition. Soft top rear seals — standard S197 inspection. Verify all power accessories (windows, convertible top motor speed). Ask about any timing chain noise on cold start.
picks.bottomLine: Most affordable Mustang option — high miles but the 3.7L is durable; verify and budget for fresh plugs and rear seal if needed.

picks.whyGood: Same spec as rank-2 (2014 V6) with slightly higher mileage but priced $995 higher — worth considering only if the rank-2 listing is gone. Private seller on CarGurus.
picks.whatToVerify: Same S197 checklist. Private seller means no dealer warranty — extra emphasis on PPI by an independent Mustang shop.
picks.bottomLine: Backup option to rank-2 at similar miles — price it down if negotiating.

picks.whyGood: Third 2014 V6 in the batch — AutoTrader listing at Discount Auto, 34 miles out. No accidents. Mirrors rank-3 on price and mileage.
picks.whatToVerify: Standard S197 soft-top and drivetrain checks. Confirm Discount Auto is a licensed dealer (verify CARFAX).
picks.bottomLine: Third option if the first two are gone — same year, same spec, furthest distance.

picks.whyGood: Lowest-priced Mustang at $8,548 — but highest mileage at 167k. The 3.7L Cyclone V6 can handle this mileage if maintained, making it a viable option for someone who just wants a fun drop-top on a strict budget.
picks.whatToVerify: At 167k: timing chain stretch noise on cold start is the key risk. Check for any blow-by at oil cap. Rear axle seal. Soft top seals and top motor speed. Budget $800–$1,200 for any deferred maintenance items.
picks.bottomLine: Highest-mileage, lowest-price Mustang — proceed only with a clean PPI from a Mustang specialist.
